Maintenance Report — MNT-0158-006

Asset: WELL-0158 (NE-08 Well 158, T350, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 03 Sep 2023 08:00 · Finished: 04 Sep 2023 21:00 · Well stopped for this job: 37 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Megan Ward · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0158-0045 on 2023-08-31 Report written: 06 Sep 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that the motor breaker kept tripping and the pump jack would not run. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0158-0045 showed the wellhead at 38.0 °C with the air at 34.2 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit.

Root cause

Moisture got into the motor terminal box and damaged the windings.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 1 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Disconnected and removed the motor.
  2. Fitted the exchange motor on the existing base.
  3. Aligned the sheaves and tensioned the belts.
  4. Checked rotation direction and motor current.

Summary of the fix: replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours; motor current within the nameplate rating and stroke rate normal. The well was returned to production.

Notes and recommendations

  • Clean the motor cooling fins at each scheduled service.
  • Summer heat raises the risk of motor trips on this field.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0158-014

Asset: WELL-0158 (NE-08 Well 158, T350, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: wellhead Work started: 28 Mar 2025 08:00 · Finished: 02 Apr 2025 05:00 · Well stopped for this job: 117 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Brian Coleman, Kevin Price Triggered by: inspection INS-0158-0126 on 2025-03-27 Report written: 03 Apr 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that the inspector saw a thin film of oil on the wellhead. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0158-0126 showed the wellhead at 25.4 °C with the air at 15.0 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The packing rings were worn and the polished rod was lightly scored. The well stayed shut in for about 3 days longer than the repair itself because heavy rain made the lease road impassable for the service truck.

Root cause

Normal packing wear.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 4 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Closed the wellhead valves and bled off pressure.
  2. Removed the old packing.
  3. Installed new packing rings and adjusted the gland.
  4. Cleaned the wellhead area.

Summary of the fix: replaced stuffing box packing.

Testing and return to service

Checked the stuffing box with the unit running: no leak. The well was returned to production.
